'''María Dolores García Cotarelo''' (born 17 August 1943 in A Coruña) is a Spanish politician.  First involved with a clandestine socialist organization back in 1975, she went on to become the Deputy Mayor of Culture of the City Hall of Granada and was charged with insulting religion.  She continued to be involved in party politics in 2017, and was honored in 2018 as one of eleven women who helped bring democracy to Granada.

== Political career ==
García Cotarelo joined a clandestine socialist organization in 1975.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.fpabloiglesias.es/archivo-y-biblioteca/diccionario-biografico/biografias/32921_garcia-cotarelo-maria-dolores|title=García Cotarelo, María Dolores|website=Fundación Pablo Iglesias|language=es|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref>  In this period, she and her then husband Ángel Díaz Sol were key figures in the Granada socialist community.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.granadahoy.com/granada/Angel-diaz-solCuando-Gordo-Granada_0_1225977687.html|title=Ángel díaz solCuando 'El Gordo' cayó en Granada|last=Hoy|first=Granada|date=2018-03-11|website=Granada Hoy|language=es-ES|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elindependientedegranada.es/politica/partido-fuerte-partido-unido|title='Un partido fuerte, un partido unido' {{!}} El Independiente de Granada|website=www.elindependientedegranada.es|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref> After the democratic transition, her political activity was able to be open as result of changes in Spain. She went on to become the Deputy Mayor of Culture of the City Hall of Granada.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1984/10/11/ultima/466297202_850215.html|title=María Dolores Garcia Cotarelo,|date=1984-10-11|work=El País|access-date=2019-04-20|language=es|issn=1134-6582}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hemeroteca.abc.es/nav/Navigate.exe/hemeroteca/madrid/abc/1986/01/30/047.html|title=ABC (Madrid) - 30/01/1986, p. 47 - ABC.es Hemeroteca|website=hemeroteca.abc.es|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref><ref name="Hernández">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ihPdBAAAQBAJ|title=Mujeres y política granadina. Una mirada a través de la prensa y la radio del último cuarto del siglo XX|last=Hernández|first=María F. Sánchez|date=2014-06-23|publisher=Editorial Dykinson, S.L.|isbn=9788490850503|language=es}}</ref>  She was on the socialist of candidates for the 1979 local Granada elections.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZXd24HFzBsgC|title=Memoria de la transición democrática en Granada|last=Mellado|first=Juan de Dios|last2=Juliá|first2=Pablo|date=2005|publisher=Centro de Estudios Andaluces|isbn=9788496337275|language=es}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.congreso.es/portal/page/portal/Congreso/Congreso/Diputados/BusqForm?_piref73_1333155_73_1333154_1333154.next_page=/wc/fichaDiputado?idDiputado=168&idLegislatura=4|title=Díaz Sol, Ángel|website=Congress|language=es|access-date=20 April 2019}}</ref> In 1982, García Cotarelo was involved with the International Theater Festival of Granada project, which rSn into  problems as a result of the political situation at the time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.granadahoy.com/ocio/Granada-pudo-Avignon_0_1251174910.html|title=Cuando Granada pudo ser Avignon|last=Hoy|first=Granada|date=2018-06-03|website=Granada Hoy|language=es-ES|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref> he proposed the ''Rimado de Ciudad'' project in 1983.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.olvidos.es/lprocesos/27/page:9|title=Olvidos.es Procesos: RIMADO DE CIUDAD: 30 AÑOS DESPUÉS|website=www.olvidos.es|access-date=2019-04-20|archive-date=2019-04-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420152337/http://www.olvidos.es/lprocesos/27/page:9|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1984, she was prosecuted for insulting religion, violating article 209 of the Penal Code, after allowing a comic depicting a priest holding up his [[cassock]] to reveal his genitals that were an inverted cross to be included in an exhibition she organized.<ref name=":1" /><ref name="a2">{{Cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1984/09/19/sociedad/464392809_850215.html|title=Concejala procesada por la exhibición de un 'comic' contra la religión católica|date=1984-09-19|work=El País|access-date=2019-04-20|language=es|issn=1134-6582}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ideal.es/jaen/prensa/20070723/vivir/historias-censura-granada_20070723.html|title=Historias de censura en Granada|date=2007-07-23|website=Ideal|language=es-ES|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref>  The comic was removed from the exhibit by Franco era councilor Eduardo Jiménez Gil de Sagredo.  García Cotarelo told ''[[El País|El Pais]]'' at the time, "The times of censorship have already passed, and from this exhibition is the municipality the only responsible."<ref name="a2" /> At the same Eme|language=es|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref> She also helped bring [[carnival]] to the city.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://granadaimedia.com/carnavales-con-historia/|title=Carnavales con Historia, en el Zaidín|last=Moreno|first=Lorena|date=2018-02-21|website=GranadaiMedia|language=es|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref> She was acquitted in June 1985.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1985/06/05/sociedad/486770409_850215.html|title=Una concejala de Granada, absuelta de un delito contra la libertad de conciencia|date=1985-06-05|work=El País|access-date=2019-04-20|language=es|issn=1134-6582}}</ref> She continued to serve in the role of Deputy Mayor of Culture in 1986 and 1987.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1986/08/29/cultura/525650403_850215.html|title=El alcalde de Granada atribuye a 'ultras' el incendio del auditorio Manuel de Falla|date=1986-08-29|work=El País|access-date=2019-04-20|language=es|issn=1134-6582}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1986/08/15/cultura/524440803_850215.html|title=La policía investiga una pista sobre el incendio del auditorio Manuel de Falla|date=1986-08-15|work=El País|access-date=2019-04-20|language=es|issn=1134-6582}}</ref>  Following a fire at the Manuel de Falla auditorium, opposition councilor Enrique Martínez Checa demanded the resignation of García Cotarelo and several others in the city government.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1986/08/14/cultura/524354402_850215.html|title=Indicios de que un atentado provocó el incendio del auditorio Manuel de Falla, según un informe municipal|date=1986-08-14|work=El País|access-date=2019-04-20|language=es|issn=1134-6582}}</ref>

García Cotarelo went on to serve as director of [[Museo Casa Natal Federico García Lorca]] for a short period of time in the 2000s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.larazon.es/historico/el-reto-de-fuente-vaqueros-OJLA_RAZON_32968|title=El reto de Fuente Vaqueros|last=Razón|first=La|date=2007-12-28|website=www.larazon.es|language=es-ES|access-date=2019-04-20|archive-date=2019-04-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420140743/https://www.larazon.es/historico/el-reto-de-fuente-vaqueros-OJLA_RAZON_32968|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was still involved in PSOE party politics in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elcomercio.es/gijon/candidatura-afines-barbon-20171105003809-ntvo.html|title=La candidatura de los afines a Barbón se perfila con un manifiesto "por el cambio"|date=2017-11-05|website=El Comercio|language=es|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ideal.es/elecciones/andalucia-2015/granada/201503/18/psoe-promovera-modernizacion-sector-20150318010309-v.html|title=El PSOE promoverá la modernización del sector agrario y aportará más fondos|date=2015-03-18|website=Ideal|language=es-ES|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref>  In 2018, she was one of eleven women honored by the Townhall of Granada for helping restore democracy to the city.  The other women were [[Mercedes Moll de Miguel]], [[Antonina Rodrigo]], [[Concepción Fernández-Píñar Lorca]], [[María Izquierdo Rojo]], [[Natividad Bullejos Cáliz]],  [[Milagros Mantilla de los Ríos]], [[Amalia Jiménez García]], [[Francisca Fuillerat Pérez]], [[Mariluz Escribano Pueo]] and [[Fermina Puerta Rodríguez]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elindependientedegranada.es/politica/granada-reivindica-papel-once-mujeres-que-construyeron-democracia|title=Granada reivindica el papel de once mujeres que construyeron la democracia|website=El Independiente de Granada|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ideal.es/culturas/emotiva-reivindicacion-mujeres-20181127231950-nt.html|title=Emotiva reivindicación de las mujeres de la Transición|date=2018-11-27|website=Ideal|language=es|access-date=2019-04-20}}</ref>

== Personal ==
Garcia Cotarelo was born on 17 August 1943 in [[A Coruña]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />  She was married to [[Ángel Díaz Sol]], with whom she has two children who are nine years apart in age.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> One was born in 1975, and the other was born in 1966.<ref name=":2" /> Her husband was born in [[Madrid]], and sources have wrongly listed his place of birth as hers.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />  She moved from Madrid, where she met her husband at university, to Granada so he could take a faculty teaching position.<ref name=":2" /> Garcia Cotarelo studied biology, and her profession before entering politics as a biologist with a focus on human genetics.<ref name=":2" />

While her name is María Dolores, she has been called a number of names including Mariló and Beatriz.  No one actually calls her María Dolores.<ref name="Hernández"/>
